_comment: Authoritative release-source list for the in-app updater (FEAT-050). The app asks EVERY entry each round and takes the highest version anyone reports — no entry can shadow another, so a stale or archived host cannot freeze updates. Order is still meaningful: on a version tie the earlier entry wins, and its URL is the one tried first for the download. Every downloaded APK is verified against its SHA-256 and against the TOFU-pinned signing certificate regardless of which entry served it, so the transport here is untrusted by design — see UpdateSource.kt. This file is the ONLY lever that can retire a release host for installs already in the field: the compiled-in defaults cannot be changed retroactively. Keep at least one usable entry, otherwise the app falls back to its embedded list.
_retiring_a_host: Removing a retired host or setting enabled:false is good hygiene — it saves every install one request per check — but it is no longer load-bearing for correctness: since the app sweeps all sources and takes the maximum version, a host left in place while frozen simply loses the comparison instead of hiding the others.

sources._note: Canonical forge. Replace url/owner/repo here when the migration lands — installs in the field pick it up within a day without a new APK. Works unchanged for GitHub: use https://api.github.com as url.

DISABLED UNTIL github.com/CruxCoach/CruxCoach HAS RELEASES. As of 2026-08-07 that repo is a ref-only mirror of Codeberg: 20 branches, zero releases, zero assets. Codeberg's push-mirror copies git refs and nothing else. An enabled entry would therefore answer every check with 'no releases' and be counted as a healthy source that simply has no update — the quietest possible failure. Enable it in the same change that publishes the first release there (scripts/publish-github-release.sh in the app repo), and verify with curl that /repos/CruxCoach/CruxCoach/releases is non-empty first.
Forge-independent. Publisher-signed NIP-82 events; assets are content-addressed, so this entry serves any release whose hash we know.
Plain release pointer regenerated nightly by tools/update-download-link.mjs. Discovery only — the URLs actually used are derived from the hash by the app.

Content-addressed download-only fallback (BUD-01 GET /<sha256>). Same public Blossom servers cruxcoach-blossom-sync already publishes board-DB chunks to. The project's own blossom-server is deliberately absent: it binds 127.0.0.1:3000 with no publicDomain and is unreachable from devices.
